 Flash floods batter Klang Valley
 Flash floods batter Klang Valley
 02-Nov-2026, 18:25 02 Nov 2026, 18:25 FMT Reporters Share The worst-hit area is Kampung Melayu Subang, where floodwaters have exceeded the danger level by 1.37m.
 Photos of flooded houses and cars in Kampung Melayu Subang shared on Threads by user @srhh_ today. (Threads pics) 
 PETALING JAYA : Flash floods have battered the Klang Valley, with several social media posts documenting the extent of the damage. 
 At 3.15pm today, the meteorological department issued warnings of thunderstorms in several states, including Selangor.
 According to the Selangor irrigation and drainage department’s Infobanjir portal, parts of the Klang Valley, including TTDI Jaya in Shah Alam, have recorded worrying rises in water levels.
 The worst-hit area was Kampung Melayu Subang, where the water level reached 18.77m above sea level, exceeding the 17.4m danger threshold.
 Threads user @srhh_ shared pictures of the flooded village at 4.54pm, showing some cars almost completely under water.
 “This uncle was unable to move his car because the area was flooded within 10 minutes. You can only see the car’s roof,” she said.
 Threads user @ikhwannasiranuar said roads approaching the Bukit Jelutong toll plaza were also flooded, leaving one side of the road inaccessible.
 According to Threads user @slmanfrish, flash floods were reported in front of Amcorp Mall in Petaling Jaya, slowing traffic on Jalan Templer.
 In a statement, the Selangor fire and rescue department said three flood victims, including a baby and a 50-year-old man with disabilities, from Kampung Subang, Shah Alam were evacuated to a flood relief centre.
 “There are flood victims who refused to leave their homes despite being ordered to do so,” the department said, adding that water levels in the affected areas were receding.
 It also said an estimated 92 homes were inundated by floodwaters.
